claude.sample_unit: LLMs evaluated on 8 clinical scenarios each with structured and vague prompts

links.outcome: Clinical adequacy of LLM-generated narrative summaries on intended-use scenarios
links.effect: Structured prompts produced clinically adequate summaries 39% vs 9% for vague prompts; none of the models reliably produced clinically usable summaries.
links.quote: None of the models tested reliably produced clinically usable summaries.

links.outcome: Clinical adequacy, hallucination and bias for structured vs vague prompts
links.effect: Both approaches conformed to instructions equally (64%). Structured prompts more often produced clinically adequate summaries (39% vs 9%) but also more hallucinations and bias.
links.quote: The structured approach was more likely to produce a clinically adequate summary (39% compared to 9%) but also more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias.
